bib.title: GLM-5: from Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering

read.skipped: reference list skimmed only; figure-embedded numbers (Figs 1-4, 11) not verified

question: How can a 744B open-weight MoE be trained and post-trained efficiently (DSA attention, asynchronous RL) to reach frontier agentic, reasoning and coding performance?
contributions: DSA adopted to cut training and inference cost, model scaled to 744B and 28.5T tokens
new asynchronous RL infrastructure decoupling generation from training
asynchronous Agent RL algorithms (TITO, double-sided importance-sampling masking, stale-sample dropping)
full-stack adaptation to seven Chinese GPU platforms

method.summary: GLM-5 is a 744B (40B active) MoE with MLA and DeepSeek Sparse Attention, pre-trained on 28.5T tokens, mid-trained to 200K context, then post-trained with SFT, Reasoning RL, Agentic RL, General RL and on-policy cross-stage distillation on the slime framework.
method.task: foundation model pre-training and post-training for agentic engineering

datasets.name: Pre-training corpus (web, code, math and science)
datasets.size: 28.5T tokens total including mid-training (introduction also says a 27T token corpus for base training)
datasets.source: web with DCLM and world-knowledge classifiers, code platforms and Software Heritage, math/science from webpages, books, papers
datasets.preprocessing: code corpus fuzzily deduplicated, 28% more unique tokens; no synthetic or template data in math/science

datasets.name: Mid-training data
datasets.size: 32K stage 1T tokens, 128K stage 500B, 200K stage 50B; issue-PR portion about 160B unique tokens from about 10 million issue-PR pairs
datasets.source: repo-level code, commit diffs, issues, PRs, books, papers, synthetic long-range data (NextLong, EntropyLong style), MRCR-like data at 200K
datasets.preprocessing: PPL, dedup, length filters; interleaved packing

datasets.name: SFT corpus
datasets.source: general chat, reasoning, coding and agent data; execution-environment trajectories
datasets.preprocessing: rejection sampling, expert RL, errors masked in loss; difficulty filter vs GLM-4.7

datasets.name: Reasoning RL prompts
datasets.split: roughly balanced across math, science, code, TIR
datasets.source: open datasets, vendor-annotated, Codeforces, TACO, SYNTHETIC-2-RL, internal pools
datasets.preprocessing: difficulty filter: GLM-4.7 solves rarely or fails, teachers (GPT-5.2 xhigh, Gemini 3 Pro Preview) can solve; binary outcome rewards

datasets.name: Agentic RL environments
datasets.size: over 10K verifiable SWE and terminal environments; SWE across 9 languages; WKG over two million web pages for search tasks
datasets.source: real GitHub issue-PR pairs via RepoLaunch, Harbor-format terminal tasks synthesized from seeds and web corpus, multi-hop QA from a web knowledge graph
datasets.preprocessing: search-question filter: drop questions a tool-free model answers in at least 1 of 8 attempts

datasets.name: CC-Bench-V2
datasets.size: frontend 220 tasks (HTML 113, React 58, Vue 49); backend 85 tasks; plus repo exploration and chained tasks

datasets.name: Public ARC benchmarks
datasets.source: HLE, AIME 2026, HMMT 2025, IMO-AnswerBench, GPQA-Diamond, LongBench v2, SWE-bench Verified/Multilingual, Terminal-Bench 2.0, CyberGym, BrowseComp(-ZH), tau2-Bench, MCP-Atlas, Tool-Decathlon, Vending-Bench 2, GDPval-AA, SWE-rebench

models.name: GLM-5
models.architecture: MoE with MLA (Muon Split, 256 head dim) and DSA, 3 shared-parameter MTP layers in training
models.heads: 64 attention heads; 32 indexer heads, indexer head dim 128

training.objective: GRPO with IcePop mismatch masking and no KL term (Reasoning RL); group-wise policy optimisation with token-level double-sided importance-sampling masking (Agentic RL); on-policy distillation with advantage log(pi_teacher/pi_train) (cross-stage); next-token plus MTP in pre-training
training.lr: pre-training warmup 0 to 2e-4 then decay to 4e-5; mid-training linear 4e-5 to 1e-5; DSA warm-up 5e-3 to 2e-4; DSA sparse adaptation constant 1e-5
training.lr_schedule: cosine decay with batch-size warmup (following GLM-4.5)
training.warmup: DSA warm-up stage 1000 steps; pre-training warmup length not stated
training.batch_size: DSA warm-up 14 sequences per step; Reasoning RL batch 32 with group size 32; cross-stage distillation batch 1024 with group size 1; GLM-4.7-Flash DSA warm-up batch 16; pre-training batch size not stated
training.tokens: 28.5T total for base model; mid-training 1T (32K) + 500B (128K) + 50B (200K); DSA adaptation 20B; efficiency ablations 190B (GLM-9B) and 150B (GLM-4.7-Flash)
training.seq_len: 4K to 200K progressively; DSA warm-up 202,752 tokens per sequence; SFT up to 202,752
training.precision: FP8 for rollout inference; INT4 QAT in SFT; training precision otherwise not stated
training.hardware: not stated for pre-training; rollout inference e.g. EP64 and DP64 over 8 nodes

other.reasoning_rl: beta=2, eps_low=0.2, eps_high=0.28, fully on-policy, group 32, batch 32
other.agentic_rl: epsilon_l, epsilon_h and staleness threshold tau not stated; optimizer reset after each weight sync to inference engine; weights pushed every K gradient updates (K not stated); over 1k concurrent rollouts; groups padded if more than half of valid samples remain, else dropped
other.indexer: frozen during RL; torch.topk deterministic operator

inference.temperature: 1.0 for HLE/reasoning and Claude Code TB2/CyberGym; 0.7 for SWE-bench and Terminus-2
inference.max_tokens: 131,072 reasoning; 202,752 HLE with tools; 16384 SWE-bench; 8192 Terminus-2; 65536 TB2 Claude Code; 32000 CyberGym
inference.samples: TB2 Claude Code averaged over 5 runs; CyberGym single-run Pass@1 over 1,507 tasks; repo exploration Pass@1 over three runs; other benchmarks not stated
inference.prompting: OpenHands with tailored instruction for SWE-bench; tau2-Bench user-simulator prompt adjusted for Retail and Telecom (Figs 12, 13)

parameters.DP_routing: consistent hashing of rollout ID to DP rank

metrics.name: Pass@1 / accuracy / resolved rate
metrics.definition: benchmark-specific; Pass@1 on backend means all 5-10 unit tests pass

metrics.name: BSR / ISR / CSR
metrics.definition: build success rate; instance success (all specs pass); check-item success rate

metrics.name: Vending-Bench 2 final balance
metrics.definition: bank balance after a simulated year

metrics.name: Accept length
metrics.definition: mean accepted draft tokens per step, 4 speculative steps

eval.protocol: Mixed: vendor-run for most; Vending-Bench 2 run independently by Andon Labs; no confidence intervals or seeds for most Table 7 scores; judges differ by benchmark

availability.weights: open weights released (HuggingFace, per the acknowledgements)
availability.data: verified Terminal-Bench 2.0 on HuggingFace zai-org/terminal-bench-2-verified; CC-Bench-V2 not stated as released

prompts.text: Do not generate the '###TRANSFER###' before agent clearly tells "YOU ARE BEING TRANSFERRED TO A HUMAN AGENT. PLEASE HOLD ON.".
Do not end until you have clearly and completely expressed all your requirements and constraints.
prompts.where: Fig 13, Appendix B.3 (excerpt of a longer prompt)

evidence.quote: GLM-5 scales to 256 experts and reduces its layer count to 80
evidence.where: Sec 2.1; Table 10 lists 3 dense + 75 MoE layers + 1 MTP

results.claim: GLM-5 scores 77.8% on SWE-bench Verified in the authors' OpenHands run.
results.setup: OpenHands, tailored instruction prompt, temperature 0.7, top_p 0.95, max_new_tokens 16384, 200K context; single reported score, run count not stated
results.table: Table 7, row SWE-bench Verified, column GLM-5

results.claim: On decontaminated SWE-rebench (January 2026), GLM-5 resolves 42.1%, level with GLM-4.7 at 41.3% and well below Claude Opus 4.6 at 52.9%.
results.setup: SWE-rebench Jan 2026 official leaderboard numbers; Resolved Rate, SEM 1.21%, Pass@5 50.0%; harness not described by the paper
results.table: Table 9, row GLM-5, column Resolved Rate (%)
results.note: Table 9 prints GLM-5 SEM 1.21% and Kimi K2.5 SEM 1.21%.

results.claim: A non-deterministic top-k operator in the DSA indexer made RL collapse after a few steps; deterministic torch.topk fixed it.
results.setup: Reasoning RL on a DSA-based GLM-5; indexer k = 2048; no numbers given, described qualitatively
results.quote: other non-deterministic top-k operators (e.g., CUDA or TileLang implementations) caused drastic performance degradation during RL after only a few steps, accompanied by a sharp drop in entropy

results.claim: Keep-recent-k=5 context folding lifts GLM-5 BrowseComp from 55.3% to 62.0%.
results.setup: BrowseComp, judge o3-mini with official OpenAI prompt, k = 5
results.quote: improves GLM-5 from 55.3%(w/o keep-recent-k) to 62.0%(w/ keep-recent-k)

results.claim: Hierarchical context management (keep-recent plus discard-all at T=32k) gives GLM-5 75.9 on BrowseComp.
results.setup: T = 32k via parameter search, keep-recent k = 5
results.table: Table 7, row BrowseComp (w/ Context Manage), column GLM-5

results.claim: GLM-5 reaches 56.2 on Terminal-Bench 2.0 (Terminus-2), 60.7 on the verified version.
results.setup: Terminus-2, timeout 2h, temperature 0.7, top_p 1.0, max_new_tokens 8192, 128K context, 16 CPUs 32 GB

results.claim: GLM-5 closes DSA vs MLA gap with 20B tokens of sparse adaptation.
results.setup: Continued pre-training from mid-trained base; warm-up 1000 steps of 14 sequences of 202,752 tokens; DSA 128k: MQ-NIAH 100.0, MV-NIAH 97.0, SQuAD 86.0, HotpotQA 63.0 vs MLA 100.0/95.5/79.7/66.3
results.quote: The sparse adaptation stage follows the training data and hyperparameters of mid-training and goes through 20B tokens.

results.claim: Search-based SWA layer selection beats fixed interleaving on RULER@128K but still loses 5.69 points to full attention.
results.setup: GLM-9B, 40 layers, 190B continual-training tokens at 64K, 1:1 efficient to full layers, window 4096
results.quote: up to 5.69 points on RULER@128K and 7.33 on RepoQA@128K
results.note: Table 5 shows RepoQA@128K delta for SWA Pattern as 14.66 and SimpleGDN as 7.33; the text's 'up to' sentence is about the narrower set.

results.claim: On GLM-4.7-Flash, DSA after 150B joint tokens is within 0.35 points of baseline at 128K RULER and above it at 16K to 64K.
results.setup: GLM-4.7-Flash with MLA; indexer-only warm-up 1,000 steps batch 16 then 150B tokens joint
results.quote: while incurring only a 0.35-point deficit at 128K

results.claim: MTP with 3 parameter-shared layers gives accept length 2.76 vs DeepSeek-V3.2 2.55.
results.setup: 4 speculative steps on a private prompt set
results.table: Table 2, row GLM-5, column Accept Length

results.claim: Muon Split lets MLA match GQA-8 (e.g. HumanEval 36.7 vs 38.5 for GQA-8 and 33.5 for plain MLA).
results.setup: Muon optimizer, orthogonalise per-head up-projection matrices separately; sizes of these ablation models not stated
results.table: Table 1, row MLA + Muon Split, column HumanEval

results.claim: Slide-generation RL raised strictly 16:9 pages from 40% to 92%.
results.setup: HTML slide generation with three-level reward, plus rejection sampling and masking

results.claim: Slide-generation RL showed reward hacking (hard truncation, spacing manipulation), fixed by patching the renderer.
results.setup: slide RL, runtime-rendering reward level
results.quote: we observe several forms of reward hacking behaviors, such as hard truncation of overlong content or excessive manipulation of spacing

results.claim: Human evaluation: GLM-5 slides win 67.5% overall against GLM-4.5.
results.setup: human evaluation, sample size not stated; content 60%, layout 57.5%, aesthetics 65%
results.quote: resulting in an overall win rate of 67.5%

results.claim: On CC-Bench-V2 chained tasks GLM-5 gets 52.3 Pass@1 vs GLM-4.7 43.0 and Claude Opus 4.5 61.6.
results.setup: internal benchmark, Claude Code harness, Pass@1 on individual tasks
results.table: Table 8, row Chained Tasks, column GLM-5

results.claim: GLM-5 build success rate on CC-Bench-V2 frontend is stated as 98.0%.
results.setup: BSR across stacks

results.claim: Agent-as-a-Judge agrees with human experts on 94% of 130 check-items; ranking Spearman 85.7% over 8 models.
results.setup: judge Claude Code with Claude Sonnet 4.5 plus Playwright MCP
results.quote: the two agree on 94% of items

results.claim: Base model GLM-5-Base improves EvalPlus to 87.0 Pass@1 vs GLM-4.5-Base 78.1 but drops on GSM8K (68.8 vs 79.4) and MATH (56.4 vs 61.0).
results.setup: few-shot base-model eval; protocol in Table 11 not described beyond metric names
results.table: Table 11, row GSM8K (EM), column GLM-5 Base

results.claim: GLM-5 scores 50 on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.0, up from 42 for GLM-4.7.
results.setup: Intelligence Index v4.0, 10 evaluations
results.quote: GLM-5 scores 50 on the Intelligence Index v4.0

results.claim: GLM-5 scales to 744B total / 40B active parameters, 256 experts, trained on 28.5T tokens.
results.setup: MoE with DSA
results.quote: This results in a 744B parameter model (40B active parameters)

results.claim: The Chinese-chip port cuts long-sequence deployment cost by 50%.
results.setup: single Chinese node (Ascend Atlas 800T A3) vs dual-GPU international cluster; no measurement details
results.quote: reducing deployment costs in long-sequence scenarios by 50%

results.claim: Reasoning RL is on-policy GRPO with IcePop, no KL term, group size 32 and batch size 32.
results.setup: beta=2, eps_low=0.2, eps_high=0.28
results.quote: Training is performed entirely on-policy with a group size of 32 and a batch size of 32.

results.claim: On-policy cross-stage distillation uses group size 1 and batch size 1024.
results.setup: teachers are final checkpoints of SFT, Reasoning RL and General RL
results.quote: the group size in the GRPO algorithm is configured to 1 to increase data throughput, and the batch size is set to 1024

limits: Most Table 7 scores are vendor-run, single runs with no intervals; run counts stated only for a few benchmarks.
Agentic RL clip bounds epsilon_l, epsilon_h, staleness threshold tau, sync interval K, and all pre-training batch/compute/hardware figures are not stated.
DSA RL findings on the top-k operator are qualitative with no curves or numbers.
Pre-training token total given as 27T in the introduction and 28.5T elsewhere (the latter includes mid-training).
Layer count given as 80 in text; Table 10 lists 3 dense + 75 MoE + 1 MTP.
CC-Bench-V2 is internal and judge-based; GLM-5 trails Claude Opus 4.5 on ISR and chained tasks.
Base-model GSM8K and MATH regress against GLM-4.5-Base (Table 11).
Text BSR 98.0% differs from Table 8 per-stack values (100, 100, 100, 95.0).
